b2plus-continuative.title: Continuative Aspect: -avermoq
b2plus-continuative.explanation: -avermoq (from -a + vermoq, "to give") marks an action continuing without stopping: u kutib turaverdi (he/she kept on waiting), gapiraverdi (he/she kept on talking). It can also soften a command into permission to continue: gapiraveringiz (please, go on talking).
b2plus-continuative.fact: Vermoq ("to give") turns up as a grammaticalized helper verb here with no sense of "giving" left at all -- it's been repurposed purely to mark that an action keeps going, one of several originally full verbs in Uzbek (bor-, ol-, tur-) that have been hollowed out into pure aspect markers.

dialogue.native: Ha, hech qayoqqa ketmay, kutib turaverdi.
dialogue.en: Yes, without going anywhere, he/she kept on waiting.

b2plus-converb-reduplication.title: Converb Reduplication for Vividness
b2plus-converb-reduplication.explanation: Repeating a converb in -(i)b back-to-back paints a vivid, drawn-out picture of an action happening repeatedly or continuously alongside the main clause: yig'lab-yig'lab gapirdi (he/she spoke while crying and crying / spoke through repeated tears), kulib-kulib hikoya qildi (he/she told the story laughing and laughing).
b2plus-converb-reduplication.fact: This reduplication is a purely stylistic intensifier -- yig'lab gapirdi (single converb) and yig'lab-yig'lab gapirdi both mean "spoke while crying", but only the doubled form conveys that the crying was repeated, drawn-out, or emotionally heightened, the way English might reach for "crying and crying" instead of just "crying".

dialogue.en: How did he/she tell the story?
Crying and crying, he/she barely managed to speak.

items.en: He/she kept on waiting.
I'll keep on working.
He/she kept on talking, nobody listened.
The child kept on crying.
Please keep resting, I'll finish.
He/she kept on writing until the book was finished.
We kept on walking until we reached the destination.
He/she kept on laughing, even before I finished speaking.
Please keep reading, I'm listening.
The child kept on playing, without getting tired.
He/she kept on searching until he/she found it.
We'll keep on waiting until he/she comes.
He/she spoke while crying and crying.
He/she told the story laughing and laughing.
He/she came running and running.
Trembling and trembling, he/she began to speak.
Thinking and thinking, he/she finally decided.
Waiting and waiting, he/she lost hope.
Writing and writing, he/she finished the book.
Asking and asking, he/she found the house.
Laughing away, he/she joked.
He/she worked without stopping at all.
Searching and searching, he/she found nothing.
Running and running, he/she finally arrived.
